title: Candidate opportunity
description: A candidate opportunity generated in the Diverge phase. Every field exists to make a specific failure mode impossible: untraceable ideas, vague mechanisms, self-graded novelty, and edge claims without assets. lint_candidate.py enforces this schema plus the deterministic slop gate.

one_liner.description: One sentence: actor + moment + mechanism + replaced workaround. Not a slogan.

status.description: Pipeline position. Lint requirements tighten as status advances; 'survivor' must pass everything.

observation_ids.description: At least 3 observations spanning at least 2 different lenses. An idea that cannot cite its observations does not exist.

actor.description: Narrow actor. 'Accountants' fails review; 'solo tax accountants filing Turkish e-invoices' passes.

trigger.description: The specific workflow moment where the product enters.

steps.description: 2-4 concrete steps describing HOW it works. Each step names an input, an operation, and an output. 'Use AI to analyze' is not a step.

replaces_workaround.description: What the actor does today instead. If nothing, the pain probably is not real.

change.description: What became possible, cheap, legal, or urgent recently.

descriptor.description: Structural coordinates used by the quality-diversity archive and the portfolio redundancy audit. Two candidates sharing all of pattern+class+actor are the same idea wearing different words.

novelty.description: Filled by the novelty prosecutor, never by the generator. See references/novelty-rubric.md.

verdict.description: Controlled vocabulary. There is deliberately no 'unique' or 'novel' value: absence of found prior art is the strongest claim this system permits.

scope_searched.description: Which query families from novelty-rubric.md were actually searched (e.g. 'exact-product-shape', 'same-actor-same-workflow', 'open-source', 'failed-products').

difference.description: The specific, checkable difference — not 'ours is better'.

closest_prior_art.description: Required non-empty unless verdict is no-close-prior-art-found (which requires scope_searched to cover at least 4 query families) or unverified.

recheck.description: Second narrow prior-art pass aimed only at the differentiation claim, run in a fresh context before promotion. Survivors require outcome 'upheld' (lint-enforced); 'overturned' sends the candidate back to prosecution with the new evidence.

criterion.description: One of the criteria in references/kill-criteria.md.

kill_tests.description: Filled in the Attack phase. A 'kill' result moves the candidate to the graveyard unless explicitly overridden with a written justification in note.

edge.description: Proprietary-edge verification. See references/edge-verification.md. Public-web-only findings can never exceed 'none'.

asset.description: The concrete asset or access path. Required for potential and above.

control.description: Why the user controls it and may legally use it. Required for credible and above.

copy_difficulty.description: Why a competent competitor cannot replicate it in a quarter. Required for credible and above.

proof_metric.description: A measurable check that the edge is real. Required for credible and above.

accumulation_loop.description: usage -> unique data/learning -> better result -> retention/distribution -> more usage. Required for compounding.

test.description: The cheapest real-world experiment that could prove the thesis wrong.

cost.description: Rough cost in time or money.

kill_condition.description: The concrete result that would invalidate the idea. Written before running the test.

lineage.description: How this candidate was derived, for the quality-diversity archive.

graveyard_reason.description: Required when status is 'killed'. Kept so later runs do not resurrect the same corpse without new evidence.
